references.text: Describes the same event at Mount Sinai where the mountain was shrouded in smoke because the Lord descended on it in fire, and the whole mountain shook.
The people experienced the thunder, lightning, the sound of the ram's horn, and the smoking mountain, and they stood at a distance in fear.
The glory of the Lord appeared as consuming fire on top of the mountain to the eyes of the Israelites.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord spoke with them face to face on the mountain, right out of the fire.
Describes how the Lord spoke from the fire, cloud, and darkness, while the mountain burned with fire.
Moses turned and went down from the mountain while it was burning with fire.
The book of Hebrews refers to this event and describes the mountain as burning with fire, shrouded in darkness, gloom, and storm.
